summary: The note describes the constitutional and statutory position of the President and the Secretary of Defense within the United States Department of Defense. It states that the President is Commander-in-Chief and Chief Executive, and that the Secretary of Defense is the principal assistant to the President on Defense matters with authority under 10 U.S.C. § 113 to lead the Department and its component agencies. The Secretary's military command authority is described as second only to the President's.
one_line: Explains the President's role as Commander-in-Chief and the Secretary of Defense's statutory authority to lead the U.S. Department of Defense.
key_facts: The President of the United States is, according to the Constitution, the Commander-in-Chief of the U.S. Armed Forces.
The President of the United States is also Chief Executive of the Federal Government.
The Secretary of Defense is the Principal Assistant to the President in all matters relating to the Department of Defense.
The Secretary of Defense's statutory authority to lead the Department is found in 10 U.S.C. § 113.
The Secretary of Defense leads the Department of Defense and all of its component agencies under 10 U.S.C. § 113.
The Secretary of Defense has military command authority second only to the President.
